diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-1 Front axle and suspension assembly
diagrams.description: Cross-sectional and component assembly diagram of the front axle and front suspension system, showing strut assembly, transverse link, compression rod, stabilizer bar, front hub, and tightening torques for all primary fasteners.

callouts.F: Steel wheel: 8 to 9 kg-m (58 to 65 ft-lb); Aluminum wheel: 8 to 10 kg-m (58 to 72 ft-lb)

measurements_and_specs: F: Steel wheel 8 to 9 kg-m (58 to 65 ft-lb), Aluminum wheel 8 to 10 kg-m (58 to 72 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: All suspension bolts and nuts should be torqued to specified values. Transverse link, compression rod, and stabilizer bar interact to absorb braking, cornering, and vertical forces.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-2 Tightening wheel bearing lock nut
diagrams.description: Torquing the front wheel bearing lock nut using a torque wrench and socket to seat the bearings.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 2.5 to 3.0 kg-m (18 to 22 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Tighten lock nut to 2.5 to 3.0 kg-m to seat the bearings prior to backing off.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-3 Loosen wheel bearing lock nut 60°
diagrams.description: Loosening the wheel bearing lock nut by 60 degrees using a wrench to achieve initial running clearance.
measurements_and_specs: Loosen angle: 60 degrees (up to 15 degrees additional if needed to align hole)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: After seating, back off 60 degrees. Align adjusting cap slot with spindle hole; may loosen up to 15 degrees more if necessary.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-4 Measuring wheel bearing rotation starting torque
diagrams.description: Measuring front wheel bearing preload using a spring scale attached to a wheel hub stud at a 90-degree angle.

callouts.90\u00b0: Angle of pull relative to center line

measurements_and_specs: Starting torque (new parts): 4.0 to 8.5 kg-cm (3.5 to 7.4 in-lb)
Starting force at bolt (new parts): 0.7 to 1.5 kg (1.5 to 3.3 lb)
Starting torque (used parts): 1.0 to 4.5 kg-cm (0.9 to 3.9 in-lb)
Starting force at bolt (used parts): 0.2 to 0.8 kg (0.4 to 1.8 lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Attach spring balance to hub bolt and pull at right angle to a line drawn through center of bearing and hub bolt.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-5 Installing cotter pin
diagrams.description: Installation and bending of cotter pin through the adjusting cap and spindle hole to lock the wheel bearing adjustment.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Spread cotter pin legs away from each other against the sides of the adjusting cap.

diagrams.file: markdown/1978 280z FSM/diagrams/FA Front Axle and Suspension/fig_fa_6_measuring_toe_in.png
diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-6 Measuring toe-in
diagrams.description: Measuring front wheel toe-in across the front wheels using a drive-on/trammel toe-in gauge.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Car must be at curb weight on level ground when measuring toe-in.

diagrams.file: markdown/1978 280z FSM/diagrams/FA Front Axle and Suspension/fig_fa_7_adjusting_toe_in.png
diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-7 Adjusting toe-in
diagrams.description: Adjusting front wheel toe-in by loosening side rod lock nut and rotating side rod.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Loosen lock nut 1 and rotate side rod 2. Left and right side rods must be adjusted equally.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-8 Standard length of side rod
diagrams.description: Dimensional cross section of the steering rack side rod ball socket and stopper nut showing standard length dimension.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 8 to 10 kg-m (58 to 72 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Distance between centers of side rods should be equal on both sides. Stopper nut end surface forms the steering stopper against rack housing.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-9 Measuring steering angle, camber and caster
diagrams.description: Front wheel positioned on turning radius gauge turntable with alignment gauge attached to wheel hub to measure steering angle, camber, and caster.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Adjust steering angle using turning radius gauge before performing final toe-in adjustment.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-10 Removing brake tube and caliper fixing bolts
diagrams.description: Disconnecting the brake tube flare nut and removing the caliper fixing bolts on the front strut assembly.
measurements_and_specs: Brake tube flare nut tightening torque: 1.5 to 1.8 kg-m (11 to 13 ft-lb)
Caliper fixing bolt tightening torque: 7.3 to 9.9 kg-m (53 to 72 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Disconnect brake hydraulic tube flare nut before removing caliper bolts.

diagrams.file: markdown/1978 280z FSM/diagrams/FA Front Axle and Suspension/fig_fa_11_removing_hub_cap.png
diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-11 Removing hub cap
diagrams.description: Prying off front wheel hub grease cap using two screwdrivers prying equally from opposite sides.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Use caution to avoid damaging O-ring under hub cap. Tap lightly with soft hammer if needed.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-12 Removing wheel hub
diagrams.description: Sliding the front wheel hub assembly off the spindle with bearing installed.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Wheel hub may be removed together with disc rotor.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-13 Removing wheel bearing outer race
diagrams.description: Driving out the wheel bearing outer race from the wheel hub using a hammer and brass drift through hub internal grooves.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Utilize two grooves inside hub to alternate drift hits around race perimeter.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-14 Removing disc brake rotor
diagrams.description: Loosening the four disc brake rotor mounting bolts to separate rotor from wheel hub.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 3.9 to 5.3 kg-m (28 to 38 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Loosen four bolts securing brake disc; torque to 3.9 to 5.3 kg-m upon reassembly.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-15 Removing baffle plate screws
diagrams.description: Removing screws securing splash baffle / dust shield plate to knuckle spindle.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 0.32 to 0.44 kg-m (2.3 to 3.2 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Loosen screws securing baffle plate in position; tighten to 0.32 to 0.44 kg-m upon assembly.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-16 Installing wheel bearing outer race
diagrams.description: Pressing or driving wheel bearing outer race into wheel hub using drift ST35300000.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Drive outer race squarely into hub until fully seated against shoulder using tool ST35300000.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-17 Lubricating points of wheel hub
diagrams.description: Cross section of wheel hub showing cavity areas and recesses to be packed with multi-purpose grease.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Pack inner cavity recess of hub and hub cap with recommended multi-purpose grease to specified level.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-18 Filling bearing cone with grease
diagrams.description: Hand packing bearing cone cavities with multi-purpose grease from grease container.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Pack cavities between rollers of each bearing cone thoroughly with grease.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-19 Filling grease seal lip pocket with grease
diagrams.description: Applying grease to the seal lip pocket of a new grease seal prior to installation.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Lubricate sealing lips and fill lip pocket with multi-purpose grease before pressing seal into hub.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-20 Sectional view of strut assembly
diagrams.description: Cross-sectional detail view of front strut cartridge assembly including internal valving, check valves, piston, cylinder, and shock absorber expansion/compression flow operation.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: The piston rod, piston rod guide, cylinder, and bottom valve are precision matched parts and must be replaced as a set if faulty.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-21 Disconnecting brake hose
diagrams.description: Disconnecting the brake hose flare nut from strut bracket and removing retaining U-clip/locking spring.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 1.5 to 1.8 kg-m (11 to 13 ft-lb)
wiring_and_connections: Brake hydraulic flexible hose and hard tube
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Tighten flare nut to 1.5 to 1.8 kg-m upon reinstallation.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-22 Removing bolts connecting knuckle arm
diagrams.description: Loosening the two bolts securing the knuckle arm to the bottom flange of the front strut assembly.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 7.3 to 9.9 kg-m (53 to 72 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Force transverse link downward with pry bar after bolt removal to detach knuckle arm.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-23 [Upper strut mounting nuts under hood]
diagrams.description: Location of the three upper strut mounting nuts in the engine compartment / hood ledge tower.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 2.5 to 3.5 kg-m (18 to 25 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Support strut with jack underneath before removing the 3 tower mounting nuts.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-24 Removing front strut Assembly
diagrams.description: Lowering the jack and removing the front strut assembly with coil spring from vehicle wheel well.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Hold strut by hand while lowering jack to prevent falling.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-25 Removing self-locking nut
diagrams.description: Compressing the coil spring with compressor tool ST3565S001 and unscrewing the top self-locking nut from piston rod.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Hook tool evenly over minimum of 3 coils. Protect body stud threads when leveraging screwdriver.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-26 Removing gland packing
diagrams.description: Unscrewing gland packing nut from top of strut casing using special gland packing wrench KV40100800 while bottom is held in vise.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Retract piston rod completely down before loosening gland packing.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-27 Removing piston rod and cylinder
diagrams.description: Lifting the shock absorber cylinder and piston rod together as a matched assembly out of the strut outer casing.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Do not disassemble piston rod guide from cylinder; handle as matched set.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-28 Exploded view of strut assembly
diagrams.description: Exploded component view of front strut, coil spring, upper seat, insulator, thrust bearing, dust seal, and bound bumper rubber.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Assemble components in strict numbered sequence. Check rubber insulator and thrust bearing for wear.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-29 Filling outer casing with fluid
diagrams.description: Pouring genuine shock absorber oil into the outer casing of the strut assembly.
measurements_and_specs: Fluid type: NISSAN GENUINE STRUT OIL or equivalent
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Strictly pour 340 cc of genuine strut oil into outer casing to maintain correct shock absorber damping force.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-30 Installing gland packing
diagrams.description: Sliding gland packing over piston rod guide using special gland packing guide tool ST35540000.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Guide protects seal lip during installation over rod threads.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-31 Sectional view of gland packing
diagrams.description: Cross-sectional view of gland packing assembly highlighting grease lubrication point on internal sealing lip.

callouts.Grease: Lubricate sealing lip with multi-purpose grease

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Lubricate sealing lip marked with grease before sliding onto rod guide.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-32 Tightening gland packing
diagrams.description: Torquing gland packing with wrench KV40100800 attached to a torque wrench.
measurements_and_specs: Gland packing tightening torque: 7 to 13 kg-m (51 to 94 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Apply torque formula adjustment when using wrench adapter KV40100800.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-33 Gland packing wrench
diagrams.description: Dimensional diagram showing gland packing wrench KV40100800 with effective torque adapter offset length 0.10 m (0.33 ft) and torque wrench length l.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Use formula C = 7 * (l / (l + 0.10)) kg-m to compensate for the 0.10 m offset.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-34 Bleeding air from strut
diagrams.description: Technician bleeding trapped air from shock absorber by cycling piston rod in inverted and upright positions.
measurements_and_specs: Rod extension before tightening: approx 120 mm (4.72 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Extend rod with spindle down, then invert and retract rod fully. Repeat until stroke resistance is equal and smooth.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-35 Strut mounting bearing greasing point
diagrams.description: Cutaway illustration of strut upper mount indicating grease application points and orientation of thrust bearing.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Install mounting bearing so that it points in correct direction. Lubricate indicated bearing races with multi-purpose grease.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-36 Installing front spring
diagrams.description: Orientation of front coil spring bottom end seated into the contour groove of the strut lower spring seat.

callouts.Lower end: Bottom coil end seated against step

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Align the lower coil tail cleanly against the seat stop before releasing spring compressor.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-37 Removing stabilizer and compression rod
diagrams.description: Underbody diagram indicating fastener locations for compression rod bracket nut 1, transverse link bolts 2, stabilizer connecting link nut 3, and stabilizer bar chassis bracket bolts 4.

callouts.1: Nut securing compression rod to bracket
callouts.2: Bolts securing compression rod to transverse link
callouts.3: Nut connecting stabilizer connecting rod to transverse link
callouts.4: Bolts securing stabilizer bracket in position

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove nuts and bolts in sequence 1 to 4 to detach stabilizer bar and compression rod.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-38 Removing transverse link
diagrams.description: Detaching the transverse link pivot pin from the front suspension crossmember.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Loosen transverse link mounting bar and separate link from suspension member.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-39 Removing knuckle arm
diagrams.description: Separating the steering knuckle arm from the lower ball joint taper stud on the transverse link.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Knuckle arm is taper fit to ball joint stud. If stuck, screw nut onto stud and strike nut with hammer.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-40 Removing transverse link bushing
diagrams.description: Pressing the rubber bushing out of the transverse link eye using press replacer set ST36710000.
components: Transverse link bushing replacer set ST36710000

callouts.ST36710000: Front Transverse Link Bushing Replacer Set

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Support eye squarely on replacer base and press bushing straight through using drift.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-41 Sectional view of lower ball joint
diagrams.description: Cross-sectional view of the lower ball joint assembly showing ball stud, seat, grease plug/nipple location, and dust boot.
measurements_and_specs: Turning torque (new parts): 75 to 125 kg-cm (65 to 109 in-lb)
Turning torque (used parts): More than 50 kg-cm (43 in-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Lubricate ball joint by replacing plug with nipple and pumping multi-purpose grease until old grease purges.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-42 Sectional view of transverse link bushing
diagrams.description: Cross section showing transverse link rubber bushing installed flush into transverse link eye, noting front-to-rear orientation.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Press bushing until outer tube is flush with transverse link eye surface. Pay careful attention to front/rear orientation.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-43 Tightening knuckle arm castle nut
diagrams.description: Torquing the castle nut on the knuckle arm ball joint taper stud with socket wrench.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 5.5 to 7.5 kg-m (40 to 54 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Torque castle nut to 5.5 to 7.5 kg-m, then advance up to 60 degrees to align slot with cotter pin hole.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-44 Removing engine mounting bolts
diagrams.description: Location of engine mounting bolts connecting engine insulator brackets to the front suspension crossmember.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 1.6 to 2.1 kg-m (12 to 15 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Support engine weight with hoist before removing engine mounting bolts. Tighten to 1.6 to 2.1 kg-m.

diagrams.caption: Fig. FA-45 Removing suspension crossmember
diagrams.description: Location of frame mounting bolts securing front suspension crossmember to chassis side rails.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 4.5 to 5.0 kg-m (33 to 36 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Tighten crossmember to frame bolts to 4.5 to 5.0 kg-m.

diagrams.caption: ST35300000 Drift
diagrams.description: Front wheel bearing outer race installing drift tool.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Used to press or drive outer bearing races squarely into front wheel hub.

diagrams.caption: ST35540000 Gland packing guide
diagrams.description: Tapered guide sleeve for installing gland packing oil seal over piston rod.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Prevents damage to gland packing inner oil seal lips when sliding over piston rod threads and shoulders.

diagrams.caption: ST3565S001 Coil spring compressor set
diagrams.description: Coil spring compressor fixture with threaded spindle and safety hooks.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Must engage at least three active spring coils securely before compressing.

diagrams.caption: HT72520000 Ball joint remover
diagrams.description: Scissor-type mechanical ball joint puller/separator tool.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Separates tie rod and ball joint tapered pins without damaging rubber dust boots.

diagrams.caption: KV40100800 Gland packing wrench
diagrams.description: Special two-pin spanner wrench adapter for strut cartridge gland nut.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Has a 0.10 m (0.33 ft) offset length; apply torque correction formula when tightening.

diagrams.caption: ST36710000 Transverse link bushing replacer (FR)
diagrams.description: Press driver and receiver set for transverse link rubber bushing replacement.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Use with hydraulic press to remove and install transverse link eye bushings flush.
